Kevin Costner has aged beautifully and his acting feels like it has matured and strengthened as well. The storyline is both wide reaching and narrowly focused at once, but it never feels half done or bouncy. As someone who has been around the big, quiet, real working ranches of deep West Texas all my life I have been eyeing every scene for nonsense. So far, the working cattle and horse scenes look pretty right to me and they have some folks who can actually ride and dont look like potatoes with styled hair in a saddle. And that scenery! Holy cow is it pretty.This is not a kids show by any stretch of the imagination. Theres grown up love scenes, cursing, and violence. I had to laugh at some of the language - sounded just like the hands moving cattle down on the mesas of my family ranch during branding season.My only complaint is the actress playing Beth. I just hate her hair and voice so much. Please.cut her bangs already. And the character of Kayces son is ridiculous. Little boys that age ought to have better manners and just generally be more aware and well behaved or banished from being allowed within a mile of the horses for everyones safety. Im watching season two now and desperately rooting for John Dutton to win this modern war with developers and whiners trying to destroy the Yellowstone.

I have to say that the first episode is pretty slow and almost lost me before it was over. However, the next two had me utterly spellbound and I binged the rest of the series in two days.This is a story about more than finding a man who may be dead or lost or just walked away deliberately. This is a look at some hard truths about marriage, loss, inner strength, courage and Africa. The story inside the story is Africa and the sheer horrors of the militia vs corrupt governments vs people just trying to eek out a day to day survival.I will certainly watch another season. I do wish the actor who plays Emmanuel forgotten his name had been given a different role.he is amazing and should have been on long term.

I stumbled into this show by accident and Im loving it. Its nice to see India portrayed with a focus on middle class rather than just the crushing poverty and filth the documentaries are so zeroed in on. India is a massive mix of both and more. This show is well shot and the actors all have chemistry together. The characters are deeper with each episode and come from all backgrounds. Made In Heaven is just a basic soap opera of course, but its fun and interesting and Im definitely enjoying it.

Holy Awesomeness! It has been years since I read this book and I was hesitant to watch the tv adaptation because these things never go well. Not this time.they got it dead right. The casting is outstanding - John Hamm as Gabriel is inspired. David Tennant though. He absolutely makes the show. He was the best Doctor and now hes upped the bar for all demons. The humor here is spot on and the writers did right by the book. Good Omens is easily the best show Ive seen all year.

I wanted to love this movie. classic rom-com set in any city thats not NYC or Seattle, hunky leading man and silly excess. Im looking for something fun and not serious in these sorts of movies, not thought provoking wisdom. Crazy Rich Asians meets those basic qualities and has some funny lines. But. It felt a little forced and that so serious, arrogant, overbearing mother was a little too over the top - she reminded me of Cruella DeVille actually. Nonetheless, this was a cute, watch it once on a rainy day movie.

Im surprised at how I have enjoyed this show. Its beautifully filmed, well written and the characters feel real. The exploration of multiple points of view fleshes out the story and the real history of the time. I am starting season two tonight with much anticipation.

I quite enjoyed this miniseries. I watched the one from BBC in the 80s I thinj, so an updated version was nice. The actors had good chemistry and the pacing is quicker in this rendition. My only issue was with the use of current music in a period drama. It was jarring and felt out of place.

I tried to watch this months ago and I just couldnt get into the pilot so I forgot about the show entirely. Two days ago I was looking for something new and tried again. This time it caught me and I binged all of season one over three days.Its fresh and funny and the setting is definitely a nice change from everything else on tv. There are some jokes that wear thin as the episodes go on, but thats true of most tv series. Ill definitely watch season two.

Ill be honest, I had never heard of this show or Megan Markel until all that wedding hoopla this year. I looked up the show finally and was thrilled to find the wonderful Gina Torres from Firefly now starring in Suits. Her prescence alone was enough to convince me to give this show a shot.Im actually enjoying this. Its smart and snarky and funny. Theres the usual slimy lawyer stereotype that every lawyer tv show relies on. However, there are interesting twists and side stories that are fresh and fun. Im willing to go on to Season two.

I watched Psych now and then on regular TV when it was on and always thought it was a cute show. My husband hated it though, so it wasnt a series I followed up with often. Now I am starting from episode one and watching all of it in order.This show is campy, cheesy and just generally light hearted fun. It doesnt take itself seriously and revels in puns and sight gags. Its a nice balance to the reality cop shows and dramas offered on most tv. Plus at an hour, you get more fun than a typical sitcom.

Its been many years since I watched an episode of ER and I had forgotten how good it was. Its streaming on Hulu right now and I picked it up from the premiere and binged all of season one. Some of the tech has not aged we, of course, but the character development and chemistry between the actors is still outstanding. The show still feels real and is still captivating.

I am an avid fan of The Big Bang Theory and was happy to see a show exploring Sheldons childhood. The potential for enormous humor is here, but somehow it just doesnt deliver. The cast lacks chemistry. Annie Potts is terrific here, but everyone else just seems flat in every scene. The story arc follows the canon set by Big Bang, but its not must watch TV for us.

Somehow, I totally missed this show for the last couple of years. Luckily, I found it on HBO GO this week. Im at the end of Season Three after binging for a couple of days. I actually started it because of the connection with Mike Judge. Im totally hooked.This show is smart, snarky, and pokes fun at all the pretensions and self grandeur of both the established giants and kitchen start ups infesting Silicone Valley. At the same time this show gives a glimpse behind the scenes of the race for the next most popular app or user program. I fully respect the specific sort of intelligence that enables the coders to create useful things out of thin air - however, I have to wonder if there shouldnt be adult supervision for most of the culture. These kids just have no clue how the tangible world that the rest of live in actually works and that definitely explains some of the ridiculously over complicated software foisted on us. BTW - those click farms in India are real. . I love the show and will keep watching it.

We started watching Lucifer in an effort to find shows weve missed in the past. Five episodes later in one day, we are hooked. Streaming on Hulu just begs for binge watching I sort of love Lucifer and his entire schtick. The writers have done a terrific job with the puns and word play. Theres a lot of humor and a little heart as well. I just dont like the Chloe character at all - shes too naive to be a cop and this drives me nuts. Maze though is.well. amazing. The chemistry between her and Lucifer and Amenadiel is so much fun. I look forward to seeing D.B. Woodside every time he makes an appearance.

I really enjoyed this movie. The dry humor and snide wit were delivered perfectly by the actors and I laughed out loud often. The scenery and locations were beautiful. The point here seems to have been to highlight the nefarious behind the scenes manipulation women had to go through for any power or control over their lives. I enjoyed the snarky one liners delivered with that exquisite British courtesy.

This is just weird. There are definitely funny moments, but the overwhelming climate is drudgery surrounding low class trash. Its slow and filmed in a deliberate hazy light to enhance the sense of dingy hopelessness. The ending shows signs of promise, but I dont see this being a regular on our TV schedule - just too much self inflicted angst.

My husband and I are like kids when it comes to animated movies - we watch them all. Ive played the game, but my husband hasnt, so he came to the movie with no knowledge of what to expect. We both laughed through out the movie and I wasnt expecting that level of humor. This is charming, clever and the voices are great. Additionally, I absolutely loved the soundtrack.

I love animated movies for lots of reasons. Pets is cute with some definite funny moments and the look at house pets having lives of their own when were not home is pretty clever.However, this story has a more menacing under tone than I care for in a kids cartoon. The "flushed pets" and their agenda was unexpected and rather dark. Talk about owner killing , really? I just wouldnt feel comfortable watching this with my five year old niece.

I just binged all of Season one and set the TiVo to record Season two. I wasnt sure this concept would be compelling enough survive more than the first season, but it has me hooked.There are some places where the acting isnt silky smooth and the plot gets a bit convoluted, but they get it together by the end of Season one. I think the overall premise of Synthetic bio-robots gaining sentience and self awareness is strong. The show has a lot of potential exploring the consequences of that self awareness from both human and synth points of view.

I was pleasantly surprised by how much I enjoyed this movie. It moves fast and sucks you in immediately and doesnt let go. Theres a lot of action, but very little actual violence. I wasnt expecting so much humor either, but there are lots of funny scenes and lines throughout. For example - We stopped for gas in FALLUJAH!?I find it perfectly plausible that not only did these two guys stumble upon a way to make money on leftover government contracts, but that it can still be done today. Getting in over their heads and breaking who knows how many international laws also rings true. Greed and rushing in with no real clue can create havoc. These boys could have made a buckets of cash for a lifetime if only they had stayed off the drugs and kept the greed to a minimum.

Ok this is not comedy genius, but its not horrible either. There are enough kitten cuteness scenes to melt even my Dog Lover heart. The plot is beyond silly and over the top, but what else do you expect from a gangster flick about a kitten?There are a few truly laugh out loud scenes and jokes - I love the entire scene in the car explaining why George Michael is legit tough guy music. The movie does run too long and the result is the entire gag the plot is based on becomes a bit tired before the end. Nonetheless, this a decent way to kill some time and let your brain rest.

Sometimes a movie just stands the test of time no matter what. The jokes are fresh and snort out loud funny no matter how often you watch it. A great movie is one where a couple of lines seep into the lexicon and stick. "Did you say two utes?"My Cousin Vinny hits all these points and then some. At first glance it might seem as if the movie is making fun of the deep South, but it never feels mean spirited. Its just a look at every day silliness from a bewildered outsiders point of view. and that is fing funny. Vinny Joe Pesci is a classic fish out of water and is brilliantly funny. As his fiancee, Marisa Tomei plays the perfect dead pan, straight man foil for Pesci. Still a riot after all these years.

My husband and I are both enormous fans of both William Powell and movies from the 30s  40s. However, The Kennel Murder Case was missing something for both of us. The lively wit and banter of the "Thin Man" series is not present here. And the cast of characters was hard to follow - suspects did things without clear motivation, that sort of thing.The remastering of the film seems fine visually. The audio is still fuzzy and scratchy, but I dont know if anything can be really be done about that.

So much better than the old BBC version. My husband and I loved that show for several years, but the last couple of seasons had lost their edge and we stopped watching. The Trio felt hobbled and constrained. No longer! The Grand Tour has revived the humor, off color snark, beautiful scenery and ludicrous scenarios with exquisite automobiles.Sure, theres some useless camp in this reboot - the weekly accidental celebrity deaths are over prepped and the new NASCAR lap driver commentary is tedious and not funny after episode two. But. the chemistry between Clarkson, May and that short guy is golden. The love of the cars shines through, the pranks feel like they stem from a real camaraderie and the traveling tent is a neat idea. Way to go Amazon for investing serious money in this show and letting the original crusty charm of the Trio just be what it is and thank you for bringing us that beautiful Aston Martin road tripping through Italy.perfection.

My husband and I both thoroughly enjoyed this movie - its been a long time since we both sat through a film without acknowledging external interruptions. The acting here is powerful and plausible by del Toro and Brolin. Their characters truly felt like men on a mission who have seen enough of the blood soaked cartel underbelly to no longer care about the finesse of certain morality issues standing between them and the final objective.The death of the head of the cartel now reaching into Arizona with a new level of extreme violence is their goal and that greater good outweighs the smaller evils along the way. Brolins character makes a comment about the simple fact that none of this would happen if 20 of our population wasnt busy snorting, smoking or injecting themselves with narcotics. That is absolutely true. Drug users are absolutely the root cause of drug violence.Kate, played by Emily Blunt, is along for the ride simply to provide procedural cover for a CIA operation crisscrossing the U.S.Mexico border. Beyond that, she literally serves no purpose except to get in the way. Her character is a stereotype of a weak, frightened, ineffectual woman. Heck, one woman to another, even I wanted to leave her behind in the tunnels. She refuses to follow instructions, sulks, drops her gun in a gun fight, deliberately disobeyed orders putting herself in and others in jeopardy and then had the audacity to whine when she suffered negative consequences as a result.My personal feeling here is that Kate was really a wasted character and served no purpose other than to have a female actress in the movie. Benecio del Toro and James Borlin could have told this excellent story without that added foolishness.

I discovered this gem by accident when a marathon of season 7 was showing on tv one weekend recently. I was hooked immediately. Im now watching every episode from the beginning with gusto. Its rare to find a horse show that is done realistically and well acted and well written. Its rare to find any show that meets all those criteria actually.The horse handling, training, riding and behavioral issues are handled and explained realistically - clearly the writers have experienced horse people on staff. The scenery is gorgeous. I appreciate that this show doesnt rely on gratuitous violence, sex or drug  alcohol use to create drama or interest. Its a show I can watch and feel relaxed during and after.

My husband and I jumped into Fear the Walking Dead eagerly and had different opinions about it at the end of Season One. He quit watching by episode three saying it was moving too slowly and felt like a soap opera. He also wanted to see Daniel in charge immediately instead of goofy Travis . I was hooked and fascinated by the initial responses to the outbreak - the chaos, fear and slow comprehension of what the world was really facing.By the time Strand takes the reins, my husband came back into the fold and started watching again. We both absolutely love Strand and Daniel and could be content with the zombiefication of Travis and Nick as soon as possible. This is a nice complement to Walking Dead at a slower, more thoughtful pace with a slightly different focus.

Ive never been a Jean-Claude Van Damme fan so I wasnt expecting much, but I was pleasantly surprised by the humor sprinkled throughout the entire episode. The acting by all parties was awkward and there didnt seem to be any chemistry between any of them except Van Damme  Felicia Rashad actually.I dont hate this show, but honestly, I cant imagine this premise lasting an entire season.retired past his prime B list actor secret spy tries to make a come back to win the heart of a girl half his age. A one time movie maybe, but 5 episodes of this will get old. What might really be funny is an entire riff on the ridiculous remakes of the classics hinted at in the pilot - THAT was hysterical!

Sci-Fi on television has been hit or miss for a very long time, but The Colony is surprisingly engaging and entertaining. Josh Holloway is definitely a pleasure to watch and he brings a sense of grit and reality to this show about an alien invasion that makes no sense at first glance. The show brings you into their world of authoritarian rule, curfews, vanishing neighbors, normal life curtailed by fear and slowly pulls back the curtain, revealing bit by bit a bigger, scarier picture. My one quibble is that I dislike Sara Callies from The Walking Dead as Katie here. I find her stiff and theres no chemistry between Callies and Holloway.  Admittedly, my view could also be tainted by her characters despicable decisions as well Nonetheless, The Colony is on our Season Pass on the DVR.

I adored the first Pitch Perfect and even bought the soundtrack for it. The sequel, like all sequels, doesnt quite live up to the original. Most of the magic and originality is gone. The humor feels forced and recycled. Well except for the horror show of the two commentators - they are hysterical together. Fat Amy and Bumper have a pretty good run together in the lake scene singing "We Belong". This is a cute little rainy day movie and its not bad, just not one Ill watch again like the original movie.

I started watching this show simply for the magnificent Laurence Fishburne and have continued to watch through both seasons because the show is both funny and smart. The entire cast has a chemistry and presence that is missing from most ensembles. The writing is timely and relevant. The show treads a line addressing multiple issues from feminism to racial questions to LGBT issues to how to keep up with your kids and social media - it would be easy for the scripts to forget they are supposed to be entertaining and not just thought provoking, but Blackish pulls it off.

I dearly loved Season One of Catastrophe and I settled down with a giant glass of tea, a bowl of popcorn, the phone turned off and binged the entire second season in one night. I almost didnt make it past the first episode though. On what planet is a familys pet dog being killed as a result of their negligence funny? However, I persevered and the rest of the show does find its footing. The chemistry between Rob  Sharon is fiery and they are excellent foils for one another. The real world problems and grumpiness they show us can be hysterically funny, cringe worthy or heart warming and sweet all in the span of five minutes. The external pressures of friends in crisis and family members who bring their own crazy and health problems into the marriage are dealt with in ways that regular people can relate to. Like others have mentioned, I do think this season has lost a bit of the charm from Season One - its just almost over the edge with the crude  tasteless gags.

This is a cute movie and has some funny moments. My husband and my niece really love Kung Fu Panda and the sequels. I am not such a big fan actually. I just dont find it nearly as clever as other animated fare out there - Shrek and its sequels are definitely funnier and smarter. However, my three star rating and the familys five star rating even out to a four star in the end. This is a family friendly movie without a doubt and certainly more palatable on a rerun marathon than Frozen on a loop when my niece is visiting!

I stumbled upon this show in Season Two by accident one day and found myself strangely swept up for an hour. When Calls The Heart isnt my usual television fare at all - I typically watch darker drama, sit-coms and science fiction, so the fact that I now have this show on my DVR schedule is surprising. The is a charm here and a sweetness that is missing in other shows today.Admittedly, this show can border on the cloying and it is predictable, but I find I am ok with that. I like the clean and wholesome atmosphere of the entire plotline. Even the bad guys are family safe. There is romance, a little action, and drama, but no overt sexual innuendo and nothing crass or tacky. The whole show is refreshing and I find myself looking forward to it as a palate cleanser between heavier, darker fare.

We really enjoyed this movie. Nonstop action and tension - plenty of bang for our streaming buck. I was surprised by how well Owen Wilson pulled off a dramatic role here and while I desperately want this man to get a haircut already, he felt like a father reaching deep to find some courage and strength in a desperate situation. The woman playing the wife here isnt a great actress - the chemistry between her and Wilson was lackluster.Having been to a few places in Southeast Asia, I can see how easy it might be to find yourself suddenly engulfed in a riot or worse with no clue it was coming. The sense of close quarters and crowding in the movie was well portrayed - zig zagging through a maze of alleys and dead ends in a monsoon at night, yeah thats scary enough without homicidal gangs chasing you. No Escape is well worth watching on a Saturday night.

Since Firefly and Farscape set the bar so high for every science fiction show that tries to follow, I am wary of investing myself in any of them. The Walking Dead is the only thing that I love to the same degree and it isnt sci-fi, but has a similar high standard for characters, dialogue and overall storyline. The Expanse is showing tremendous promise. I read the first book in the series Leviathan Wakes and thought that the Rocinante and her crew had a faint Firefly-esque feel. a loose group of misfits with a common goal standing on the raggedy edge surrounded by a mystery beyond their pay grade.The tv version has done justice to the visuals described so far in the book and they have held more closely to the book than I expected with regard to the storyline. There are some changes to some of the characters and their importance and how they interact with others. Im not sure how the idea of having Holden have such an antagonist relationship with Amos, Alex and Naomi works - they were a better team in the book. Nonetheless, Sci-Fi Channel has finally decided to get its act together and produce television that is actually worth watching and even worth looking forward to again.

I usually dont like musical movies at all. My rule is "Sing me a song or tell me a story, but do not do both at once". Pitch Perfect is one of my very few exceptions to the rule. Anna Kendrick is gorgeous with a lovely voice and even better comedic timing and facial expressions. The rest of the cast is good and the writing here is well done. Its a classic college rom-com without all the angst that genre typically has. The songs are great and I like this enough that I actually bought the sound track.

This has some definite potential. The characters are interesting and the setting is certainly interesting. The comparisons to Mad Men are inevitable and Good Girls Revolt doesnt live up to that masterpiece in acting, writing or cinematography, but taken on its own, this is fine. This show is rougher, less polished and comes at the 1960s from an entirely different point of view. Mad Men was martinis and fur coats - Good Girls Revolt is LSD and hippies.I loved the juxtaposition between Jane and Patti and I especially like seeing Jim Belushi here as Wick, the establishment boss. My one star deduction is for the character of Nora Ephron. Shes so abrasive, so resentful, and so pushy, I just had no interest in watching her at all. And I cant help but feel like her issues are overblown simply for the name value she brings to the show. However, I would watch another couple of episodes.

I love this movie. It was an unusually open look at the options available to the elderly who arent well off and not sick enough to be abandoned in a nursing home. Hollywood typically ignores those stories, but this charming film addresses many hard issues and some more modern questions. The Marigold Hotel has an outstanding ensemble cast of great actors with generational talent and experience to bring to each character. The humor and chemistry draws you in and holds you. With no violence, gratuitous vulgarity or special effects as crutches, this is just good storytelling.

I was excited to watch this for the first few minutes and then I just felt lost and frustrated the longer it went on. I love period shows and those based on real people can be fascinating when done well. This could be excellent - the filmography and sets are gorgeous and the idea is intelligent and worth following through with. But the two deal breakers for me are the fake, over the top Southern accents by the actors. This is distracting and obnoxious enough to drag my attention away from whatever the dialogue may be and take me entirely out of the story. Second is the simple fact that Christina Ricci is much, much too old to play the teenage ingenue. Wasnt Zelda supposed to be 17 or 18 years old at this point in her life? Ms Ricci certainly is not and it shows. Shes not old, but shes not a teen or young 20 something either Recast with age appropriate actors and better voice coaches and I would watch again.

I absolutely hate the greed of the studios and actors involved in these book series to movie adaptations. There is simply no reason to divide the third book into two movies. Its a money grab and nothing else. This part one of Mockingjay is pretty true to the first third of the book and as such, moves slowly and does not bring any real forward movement for the conclusion of the story. This movie serves two purposes. First to remind that the Capital and President Snow are evil and vicious - we knew that from the first two moviesbooks. Second is to establish that District 13 is well armed, well fed, organized and prepared to go to war with Snow. This isnt a bad film. It is drab and dreary, without as much action and very little excitement compared to the first two installments.

Definitely an unusual idea and execution for a television show. The actor playing Highston has a quirky, charming face  expression and hes very appealing. The overall feeling here is a sweet family who is trying to figure out how to make the best of the weirdness in their much loved son. Theres definitely humor and hope throughout the episode. I would watch more of this, but I wonder how long the gag can be carried - Highston walking around talking to multiple invisible celebrities that only he and the audience can see. Shaq and Flea arent going to carry this on their own for more than a few episodes.

This is not the show for the Zombie purist. Its not the show for those who want high brow storytelling and drama with some apocalyptic zombie action as a bonus. Nope. Z Nation is just culty, gory, sometimes absurd, over the top, darkly funny zombie chasing end of the world come what may. I started watching Season One on a sick day binge and was hooked. Murphys character makes me laugh in every episode and now hes making zombie go-go dancers dance on command.this is definitely a Sy-Fy Channel production.

Frasier is one of the rare shows that remains funny and smart even 10, 12 and more years later. The writing is intelligent, the chemistry between the cast is palpable, the humor never relies on lazy vulgarity or violence, and there is always a sense of both the urbane oneophile and the Lazboy beer drinker in every episode. Season six saw Daphne engaged to Donnie and Niles aghast from afar. Frasier couldnt keep his two girlfriends straight in his head and runs in circles. Roz and Bulldog lose their minds briefly. A good season.

I finally watched this movie on one of the cable movie stations the other night and it was terrific. I wasnt expecting the humor at all - this is really funny and the characters are fleshed out with smart dialogue and enough chemistry between them to keep an adult interested. There are plenty of special effects and lots of cool sci-fi things as well which is a definite plus. As a confirmed sequel hater, I cant believe Im saying this, but I hope they make a second one - I want to know if Groot grows out of the pot!

I have been catching up on all the popular teenYAdystopian book to movie adaptations and frankly, I like The Maze Runner best so far. It has better acting by far than Enders Game and much better visual presence than Divergent and I like the story line as well as Hunger Games.Admittedly, some of the plot points from Maze Runner feel very much like these other stories. From Hunger Games - the group dynamics, the elevator with supplies, and the gamesmanship element. From Enders Game - the training and final answers about why they are in the maze to begin with. From Divergent - the idea of the one person who is special and "above and beyond" the others and can find the one answer that no one else knows. But.you know, it just works here. The action is good, the special effects are great and end took me by surprise. One star deduction for YET another sequel. Ugh.can we just get a single self contained story once in awhile?

I liked the book as a whole, but detested the weak ending. I had hoped that following the Hollywood tradition of changing things for film adaptations, Hollywood would fix the ridiculous ending. Nope. The one time the movie doesnt alter an ending when they should! I just came away feeling unclean and disgusted by both Awful Amy and Nitwit Nick. The first two thirds of this story is solid and has a very classic film noir vibe. It moves quickly and each layer peeled back reveals more rotten layers beneath in each character and you want desperately for someone to die horribly at the end - it almost doesnt matter who. Yet, as with the book, the story just fizzles out and there are no consequences for any one.

Tremendously moving. The juxtaposition between the life of a soldier in country, on duty, on gaurd 247 vs the life of a husband, father doing ordinary, gentle things was handled with a true grasp of the difficulty in making that transition. These men are expected to do incredibly difficult, dangerous work and do it with honor and courage and ferocity. Rotation home can be equally hard and fraught with invisible emotional barriers they arent able to share. Clint Eastwoods direction here was impeccable and Bradley Cooper took my breath away. I commend Mrs. Kyle for letting her story be told as well here, her journey has been long and filled with love and pain, but her husbands honor is hers as well. I stood on the side of the interstate to pay our respects to the family that day as the funeral procession rolled by enroute to Dallas. When a hero is real, real people know and remember.

I watched episode one with low expectations, but I found myself oddly fascinated and utterly swept up in the background stories of these women and our country. The addition of actual news footage and photos to the created, modern film is well done and seamlessly blended. Theres something very sweet and positive about this show that I really enjoy. I hope it stays on - its a breath of fresh air compared the other same old cop, game and reality shows.Edit on 7-31-15  The loss of the Gus Grissom in tonights episode brought me to tears. The courage of those men at that time was equaled only by that of their families. This show is handling it very well.

Wow. Something on TV thats new, different, creepy, and a offers a mystery that doesnt involve your usual murdersuper copsexy lawyer tropes! And with Matt Dillon - very nice to see him back again. Ive had the books sitting on my Kindle for a year or more without reading them yet and now Im glad I havent gotten to them yet. Im loving the suspense and angst of trying to figure out what is wrong with the town, who is calling when everyone freaks out and MUST answer their telephones, what sort of mass crazy compels an entire town to have a public "reckoning"? Excellent!

Ok.I LOVE space opera television more than any other genre. I am willing to give this show several episodes to grow up and get it together simply because there isnt anything else on like it right now. Having said that.are they kidding with the almost blatant copycat - nay, thievery from Firefly?The characters are ripped straight from Joss Whedons genius and beloved show. The female 1 is a weaker, less funny and less well rounded version of Zoe down to her low slung double hip holsters. The male 3 is a duplicate of Jayne down to carrying the big gun that looks a lot like "Vera" from the Mrs Reynolds episode of Firefly and his me  the cash first attitude. The female 4 is a dead ringer for River Tam with her weird dreams and spooky ability to understand complex electronic things "beyond her years" and talk of her lost brother whom she was very close to. REALLY?. The male 5 is a sensible, thoughtful, quiet, calm but tough in a fight when pushed black man.ummm.remind anyone of Shepherd Book? Now there is a slight twist with the Android - shes a replica of 1 of 9 from the Borg in Star Trek Next Generation. They even look alike!And then theres the ship, the Maurader. With its shuttles that are shaped suspiciously like the Serenity shuttles in Firefly. Not to mention the layout of the dining area for the crew - long wooden table and family style meal in a small, intimate room. About two thirds of the way through episode one, we learn about a big bad thing in the universe.The Raza. Rumor has it that the Raza are mutated men or alien crosses that kill and mutilate people horrifically and are feared universally. O.M.G. Say it with me folks. REAVERS. Firefly did these things first. All of them, even the smuggling angle.I appreciate a loving nod or respectful tip of the hat from a new show to the great ones that came before it. An acknowledgement of the foundation laid before. But Dark Matter better get its own ideas and fast before that tip of the hat becomes a joke and no one watches.

Jurassic Park is one of my favorite books and the first movie is a beloved classic for many reasons. The second two movies were trash. We bit the bullet, fell for the hype and spent real cash in the theater for the first showing at the 1pm matinee today of Jurassic World. I wasnt sure if this was just a reboot of the original movie or some mish mash of that and some newer special effects for the 3-D audience. The plot is the same as the first movie - two kids lost in the park, rowdy big predatory dinosaur on the loose, man  woman with loose romantic connection trying to rescue them before big dino or raptors get them. There are a couple of very minor changes and new dinosaurs. There was plenty of very bad acting throughout - primarily from the very stiff leading lady, Bryce Dallas Howard. Chris Pratt was fine, but watching him try to salvage scenes with her was almost sad.Had the plot centered on Pratt and his work with the Velociraptor pack, leaving out the entire romantic subplot with the Claire character and the ridiculous, go nowhere InGen military secret weapon subplot entirely, this would have been an awesome movie. As it was, we and others in the theater were groaning out loud and laughing at some of the more preposterous "abilities" of the newest dinosaur in the park. Additionally, entire scenes were almost direct replays of scenes from the first movie - that felt like a loving tip of the hat the first time and just weird the third time. Honestly, dont pay premium theater prices to see this. The special effects and CGI are worth the 7 matinee price, but no more. Sigh.I really, really wanted to love this movie.

I loved the book and the movie did a great job bringing some of the zombie hordes to "life" if you will. The special effects here are excellent and the tension is taught and keeps you focused. This isnt high art or social commentary, its just good movie fun. Zombie fans and action fans should enjoy World War Z for what it is - buttery popcorn, late night, tequila shot fun.

I expected a high caliber, action driven sci-fi movie with aliens and loads of special effects. I have never read the books, so I went into the movie with a clean slate. The special effects were nicely done and the idea behind the story fit in with the recent trend of adolescents saving the world in some way. Even without reading the book, I felt the characters were flat and the story was rushed - as if they were trying to squeeze way too much stuff into too little time. The result was a movie that just dragged in places and was slow yet things were happening behind-the-scenes that we had no clue about. Harrison Ford was solid here, but not at the top of his game either. To be honest, if a sequel is coming for this one, well probably pass. But.Im inclined to read the book.

We rarely spend actual money going to the theater to see a movie - maybe twice a year if that often. However, two genres draw us out of the house - disaster flicks and dinosaurs. I cannot resist a disasterapocalypse big budget movie and San Andreas certainly fit the bill. The CGI effects were excellent and the tension was exactly right for this genre - not too ramped up and the slower parts didnt make you wonder where your action film had gone.The acting was solid all around - even the supporting cast was respectable. Dwayne Johnson has grown and matured over the years and his skills are improving with every movie, I really enjoyed him in San Andreas. He felt like a Dad and a husband here, not just an all powerful hero to save the day. I do wish we had a little less of the Sci-Fi channel type plot devices in this movie -the broken family reconnecting, the ignored scientists now proven correct, the romance that springs from shared experience. All in all - fun movie and family friendly with no sex, no crime type violence and relatively little cursing.

Without giving away spoilers, the finale was ridiculous and ruined the rest of this series for me. We had pretty much enjoyed it and felt the story was being told in a gripping and well plotted manner. The characters had some issues in places, but nothing that took away from what was otherwise a darn good show. And then the ending.really? What happened.sudden urge for Starbucks in the writing room and yall just scribbled down the first bad things that popped out and called it good? A four star show that sank into the two star pit alongside Random Housewives of Absurdity.

I like the idea of this story and the theme in general - its very trendy for a reason. The plucky young girlboy in a dystopian future finding an unconventional way to break the mold and save the community from the "big bad" while discovering adventure and true love along the way. However, Divergent the movie just didnt live up to other offerings in the genre. It was very colorless in both literal color and dialogue. Some of the acting was stiff even from the experienced supporting cast. The pacing was unnecessarily slow and drawn out - the entire movie was about 45 minutes too long. Watching at home on streaming we made a snack and let the dogs in  out without pausing the movie and were able to step back in without missing a single key plot element. Hunger Games and others are lively, action filled, and colorful with excellent acting throughout - Divergent just doesnt live up to the standard.

I started watching The Royals on a lark because I adore Elizabeth Hurley. Turns out, she is excellent, as expected. The rest of the cast is hit or miss - the King and Prince and Ophelia are great and the chemistry there between the actors is good. The three Princesses are just flat and every time any of them are on screen I catch myself checking my phone or the cable guide. This show is soapy, predictable, relaxing fun and Ill set the TiVo to record season two.

It doesnt take a rocket scientist to know that the better you can eat, the better you will feel.Of course, broccoli is better for you than donuts, but . donuts!But sometimes, we need to know WHY, instead of just being told to put something down.I know a lot about nutrition and a lot about body processes. I am hypothyroid, and basically have had to learn everything I could medically to try to help myself, because doctors seem to blow off questions about thyroid function. Im overweight, and have been told some of the most unbelievable whopper stories from doctors you would ever believe. I had one actually tell me that I just had "elbow disease", saying my elbow bent to my mouth too often. Um, no. My tiny mother in law could eat more food than I could hold in two days and still stay tiny. There were obviously other factors in play here, but no one ever had any real answers - just the standard "eat better" and "exercise more".I also went on a low fat diet for about six months, and gained steadily the entire time, despite eating sparse plates of food, things like yogurt and grapes for lunches, etc. My dr blamed me, saying I HAD to be eating more than that. I wasnt! But heaven forbid we look deeper than the surface! And when I told him that I didnt feel good when I ate fruit, I was told that was complete nonsense, and that I was making things up just to go off my "diet". To this day, fruit gives me a sugar rush that is very unpleasant! I also dont like pies or cakes, but thats just me - I never liked them. But wave a cookie under my nose, and you have my attention!I also made changes myself simply because there was zero logic behind some of the "medical breakthroughs", like not eating eggs and making an enemy out of butter. I just could not see how butter, made from all natural ingredients from a cow, could possibly be worse than the chemical cocktails whipped up, dyed yellow and sold as butter flavored margarine! No freaking way. So, we ignored the medical release hype and ate real butter, eggs, meat gasp, and did away with all low fat or diet drinks. Common sense tells you that if they remove the fat from a food, SOMETHING has to replace it so it doesnt fall apart or taste like cardboard. They DO replace the fat - with sugar!This movie goes WAY below the surface, and gives you a real experience with the world of sugar. Weve long known that too much sugar could be bad for you. But other than cavities, WHY avoid it when it tastes so good? And yes - I know many dont think it tastes good - you are missing the point, so please spare the arguments about bad tasting sweet stuff.Damon walks us through the rapid and shocking changes our bodies experience when we give it the everyday diet of typical foods off the grocery store shelves. He doesnt eat candy, donuts or cake. He goes on a month long experience of eating what we normally put in our shopping carts under the guise of "healthy" food. Things like fruit juices, yogurts, health bars, chicken with teriyaki sauce, etc etc.Now, I am very aware that many foods load it with sugar to make the chemicals palatable. We became serious label readers after my husband took a year of culinary classes at an area college. Thats when we started to realize the lab experiments being sold as food that loaded our grocery shelves.I was STUNNED by the amount of sugars hidden in our everyday foods on the shelf! Reading labels changed the way we shopped, but we still were not feeling our best. Despite no longer buying some things like dare I mention brands? Hamburger Helper or Yoplait yogurt, which has so much sugar, you might as well have ice cream, we felt sluggish most of the time. We cooked more at home, choosing to control more of what we put into our bodies.But we still didnt feel our best. There HAD to be more to this, and while I had been trying to do some of my own research as to WHY my body acted like I was the enemy, and preferred to pack on weight instead of releasing it.Enter this movie.Damon - THANK YOU!Seeing what is taking place in our livers was a real eye-opener. Yes, we hear about diabetes either type, triglycerides, cholesterol, etc etc, but the medical community often wants to give you a pill to control the symptoms, instead of explaining what is truly happening and helping you to fix it. After all, medication is highly profitable!I learned a LOT from this movie. I have watched it twice, and will watch it several more times to get the information ingrained in my brain.Damon is every personable and likeable, and the movie is well done - no yawn-worthy droning documentary-style fact recitation. He interacts with the viewers at every step in a very creative manner.I cannot recommend this film highly enough. I am making everyone in our house watch it at LEAST once, if not more.Our bodies are so adaptable to changes, and it was both a wow factor and encouraging how quickly things went downhill in his health, but also how quickly things went back to normal after returning to the sugar free foods he previously enjoyed. Now, I dont have Damons metabolism and mobility, but there are certainly things that I can incorporate into my daily life to begin the reversal of what could truly be called sugar poisoning with being too far off!Again - thank you Damon.You did us all a great service!

Gotta love Leslie. She helps me to keep moving, keep motivated, and increase my general sense of wellness. I have lost and gained weight several times through my life. While I am an active person, I dont always watch what I eat. So while exercising has little direct impact, there are so many other health benefits, that it indirectly, positively impacts weight loss goals and definitely overall health. Just getting up and moving can reduce appetite, reducestabilize blood glucose levels, increase lung, heart capacity, increase strength  endurance, increase muscle which burns more calories at rest, ie more biologically needy, and improve moodcalmnesslife outlook. And so, whenever I am regularly including Leslie Sansone Walk at Home workouts in my life, I tend to make better decisions all around, and feel better. And yes, I definitely lose weight too.I always choose Leslie over other workouts. I am more apt to grab an older DVD, than newer stuff. I prefer the use of regular every day people from different walks of life, different fitness levels, and different levels of enthusiasm lol- seriously, I really do love seeing the occasional grouchy face over the cliched smiles plastered on some work out video people faces. Im not totally into super cheerful over the top excited work out leaders. Leslie can get excited, but dang. she is so stinkin authentic. I feel like I am walking with a real person when she is on screen. Her comments are helpful. Not perfect, some snafus are kinda funny, totally normal feeling. Clearly not overly produced. I am drawn to that!That being said, I have absolute favorite work outs 3 mile heart healthy, 3 miles weight loss, and I have some that I almost never use miracle miles 5 dvd set. THIS one is somewhere in between. I like this for when I am ready to change it up a bit, and get a few added different styles and energy that the others I do nearly every day. I dont care for the dance segment. Even though it isnt exactly complicated, I am terrible at coordination in watching dance moves. Fortunately it is only one short segment. The lower body can be a little taxing on my body. I cant exactly do lunges without hurting my lower back, so I either skip that, or I do squats or something else in place of that activity. Everything else is excellent for me. LOVe the arm work out- I am always amazed at how much that helps my arms and overall feeling of strength and oddly, seems to boost my caloric burn over lower body stuff.I figure, it cant hurt to add this to your collection. Add as many as you can- so many to choose from. Then, choose at random, or choose based on how youre feeling that day. Even if it is a near similar workout, the commentary, stage, dress, people, energyvibe is always different. Kind of like taking a work out class, but in home.I like this one, not my fave, but definitely a welcome addition.

I cant believe I never wrote a review for this Leslie Sansone walk at home DVD. First, I love her videos. I have only been walking with her since 2015, and I wish I would have given her stuff a try well before then. I find her walks a game changer in how much added activity I have in my day, and how much better I feel. Very functional, easy workouts that have added benefit beyond exercise. Second, I love her authentic commentary. I am not one for needing constant huge smiles, super saccharine cheer, or mega coordination. I just want it real- and this video really embraces that her older stuff tends toward that. Different bodies, ages, levels of fitness. I love seeing everyone doing this workout at their own level of exertion. It is actually helpful to see regular folks huffing and puffing, sweating, and not always having a big smile plastered on the face.This is one that has a little more movement, particularly in the middle mile which is what adds great appeal. It definitely amps up the workout. High energy. but still easy to follow! Overall I find it well balanced, and I always feel good afterward.I know many of her newer videos include a greater amount of the cliched work out enthusiasm using people already in shape good on them, and this style is certainly appealing-but I find that I rarely grab for those videos, as well as slightly more coordination, and dance like moves. I avoid those. Give me some old school Leslie. Also. even though some are slightly lower key, each set of moves can be modified a bit to get a bigger burn or lesser, depending on your needs.

I tell you what, I enjoyed this film a lot more than The Last Jedi.Its always fun to watch a low budget sci fi film. Ive heard the estimates for this one were around 80K, so the results are pretty impressive bearing that in mind. The plot centers around a fairly ambitious space mission that involves only one guy traveling to Titan, a moon around Neptune Ive forgotten which, and Eris the dwarf planet beyond Pluto. Hes looking for spheres that are apparently transmitters from some extraterrestrial intelligence. Its got quite a bit of 2001 mixed in, but not so much that you feel like this film is a rip-off.With low budget films like this, there are only a few actors. Brandon Ray Olive is the main face of the film, and he is solid as Commander Roger Nelson. Actually, the casting for that part was critical as the film would have been unwatchable without a decent lead. K Danor Gerald as Becker seemed to get some weird stage direction as hes always talking like hes hiding something, and not hiding it very well.The sets are creative enough, but you often get the sense that Commander Nelson is just sitting in a room with three ring binders velcroed to the wall. There are a few effects sequences that are only okay, not so terrible as to destroy the film. Honestly, you often see some spectacular special effects on YouTube.but who knows the budget for those shorts? Perhaps hundreds of thousands are spent on 2 minute clips, twice the budget of this whole film.The plot is actually pretty good and the scenes where Nelson explores distant moons are well done. I thought the actual concept of the mission was a bit ridiculous since his timetable often only leaves him a couple hours to fly down to a planet, explore, retrieve an alien artifact, and then hit his launch window to the next objective, but hey, its a movie and you need a counting clock.The sub plot with Commander Nelsons wife is actually a good touch and adds some necessary drama as well as a human element. When the ships computer inevitably goes on the fritz 2001 again, it doesnt play out as you might expect.I watched this last night on a fluke because I didnt feel like going to bed and am glad I did. Its a good film for an evening where you want something different from the typical big budget nonsense thats out there.

Probably some spoilersWith the possible exception of The Dark Knight, I dont believe these super hero films are masterpieces. Most of them are kind of silly, and the fact that theyre all on a carefully conceived thirty year master plan to squeeze as much money out of the general public is kind of off-putting. However, I do find the DC movies with their darker tone to be a bit more engaging than what Marvel offers.The critics have been hard on these movies but although their criticisms are consistent they dont seem to be intellectually honest. There is plenty to nit-pick in the DC films, but the critics seem to keep their objections vague in accordance with a general perception rather than point out individual flaws.Suicide Squad is a pretty solid little movie that does a couple interesting things. The actual super hero component of this film is subdued, as the characters go without masks for the majority of the film. I happen to like that, as I pay to watch actors perform, not CGI rendered suits. For that reason, I really enjoyed Iron Man 3 which showed Robert Downey Jr. playing the most vulnerable manifestation of his character.In an era where there is a constant call for Strong Female Characters” Harley Quinn is an interesting anomaly. She really steals the show here and even manages a bit of dignity despite the fact that her whole character is something of a male fantasy. Im not overly impressed with Margot Robbie as an actress, but all she has to do to effectively portray Quinn is laugh and try to be seductive. Shes interesting though because shes a sex kitten that intimidates men because of her over pronounced desire. The fact that shes wresting power away through the magnification of the typical malefemale interaction is compelling. The only scene that kind of bothered me with her was the dream sequence in which she revealed all she really wanted was a normal life. I dont think thats the fundamental desire of Harley Quinn, although I couldnt substitute what I think she really would like. The reveal that she wanted a regular life kind of felt dis-empowering. By the way, I watched this film with my wife and she preferred Harley Quinn to all the other characters by far.Will Smith does his typical star routine which is effective but as bland as yellow cheese. He plays one of those assassins who kills mafia king pins, etc., so although what hes doing is technically illegal, hes essentially the Punisher and people can relate to him. Plus hes got a little girl.the go two heart tugger to show deep down hes a kind and gentle ruthless assassin. Theres nothing objectionable to his performance, and I liked the scene where their handler assassinates a bunch of her underlings just to keep the operation covert. Im not sure the film was making the handler a good guy or not, but I think its interesting that there is a huge outcry over depictions of Batman being overly violent, but nobody bats an eye when a government official does the same. At some point people are going to have to realize that the cynicism of these DC films are reflective of a deeply felt current sense of cynicism towards our own government. Truth, Justice and the American Way” just sounds like another con to a generation of kids who cant find a job and are labeled as entitled” even though theyve got to pay off their parents 20 Trillion dollar debt.I have to spend a few seconds talking about Jared Leto. He had the toughest job in this film bringing the Joker back to life and I thought he gave a solid effort. In some ways Id say its a safe” performance since he doesnt break radically from the comic book representation as you could argue Ledger did.though Im not a comic book expert so feel free to disagree. I still dont feel a great Joker has made his way to the screen. Leto tries for menace with growls and hoots, but I think the smile kind of gives him away. There are people out there who can smile and have it appear terrifying, and Leto doesnt have a smile like that. Honestly, Id like to see a more reserved Joker. I think the menace has to build, the audience should sit there thinking, when is he going to laugh, when is he going to laugh?” and when he does it should peel the skin from their bones. A Joker laugh should be used about the same as Bond, James Bond” it has to mean something when it happens, I want to feel a little more torment from the character. However, I dont mean to detract too much from what we get. This is a very solid Joker.I thought the overall driving conflict of the film was a bit on the bland side. It seemed like sort of a generic world ending threat that was just sort of tacked on. This film starts out as a kind of 7 Samurai” as the handler puts together her Dirty Dozen” just in case the next Superman to manifest happens to be bad.” The early scenes introducing us to the Suicide Squad are the best. There have been some critics who claim the film suffers from two personalities, but I didnt get that impression. If another cut of this film exists Id be interested in seeing it, but what we have works well.The sequence in this film that sets it apart, however, is the moment when El Diablo rejects the temptation dream sequence. Everyone else is being temporarily subdued by a vision of their deepest desire, for El Diablo this is a glimpse of a life with his wife and children that he burned alive. He is able to break the spell of the vision because he knows it is impossible to overturn that act. I thought that was a fascinating comment on guilt and remorse and the toll it takes on your whole psyche. It basically crammed the whole emotional impact of The Machinist into one thirty second moment which is impressive.So dont listen to the other critics. Theres plenty to like in Suicide Squad. Its a dark, mature film that taps into emotions Marvel seems to fear.

Last night I took my two girls who are 6 and 3 to see the film version of Roald Dahls The BFG. Were in Peru at the moment, so we watched the film dubbed into Spanish. This was actually kind of fun because Roald Dahl dearly loves playing with language, and The BFG is probably the work where he indulges himself the most in this respect.Ive always been a great admirer of Dahl, and Ive only recently finished reading all his works to my daughters so the story was still fresh in their minds. Dahl gets unfairly criticized for his use of reoccurring themes like: "poor people are morally superior to rich people" and "evil people should be punished." I find it odd that Dahl would be criticized for paraphrasing The Bible but I guess most people dont read that either.Although Im a big fan of Dahl, The BFG is probably my least favorite of his works. For me, the best is Danny the Champion of the World which a lot of people havent even heard of. Matilda, Charlie and the Chocolate Factory, and James and the Giant Peach are all great, but The Great Glass Elevator, and Georges Marvelous Medicine are a tier below.My problem with The BFG is that too much of the entertainment is just how the BFG talks. Yes, it is funny, but after a time the language games start becoming a little self-indulgent. But thats just my perspective and I see and respect how other people absolutely love this book. I dont consider it a Dahl classic though.The film is quite beautiful but I have to wonder how much of it was actually "Directed" by Steven Spielberg. Hes at the point now where he can just hire a young, upcoming director to do the work and then show up on set four or five days before racking up the credit. I think there is some sort of rule about how you have to shoot 51 of the film to call yourself "The Director" but every rule can be worked around.There arent a lot of Steven Spielberg type moments. He likes to do things like point the camera at a mirror and then you see the action in the mirror.kind of self-indulgent just like the word play complaint I had before. What Spielberg is really good at is capturing the childadult relationship, and that doesnt really come across here. Although maybe my impression comes from the fact that Im watching this as an adult now and not a child. Come to think of it, Spielberg hasnt done any kids movies for a while has he?The actor playing the BFG is spot on. He does a good job with wry smiles and emoting sad kindness. Sophie is also pretty good, though a lot of her performance is just her staring over the rims of her eyeglasses.I thought the film really missed the mark with the giants though. They were a little too big and creepy and not ridiculous enough. I think Dahls weird sense of humor is the hardest thing to transfer to film. In his books, its funny when an evil school teacher grabs a child by the hair and swings her in circles before launching her over a fence. Yes, you wouldnt think a scene like that would be funny, but somehow Dahl makes it so. However, if you try to convert that scene to film and play it straight, it comes across as super creepy.The giants are a bunch of evil bullies who pick on the BFG, so you had the option for an important message there, but I think this film focuses on the value of friendship a little more, so it kind of falls flat. It does a good job hitting the plot points of the book, but I think the ending is a mistake. As I recall, the evil giants were sentenced to live in a pit, in this version they send them off to an island, forgetting that the giants have a magical running ability which allows them to cross the earth in a single evening I presume that includes the ability to run across water.The fuzzy drink that the BFG loves is well employed and if youre into fart jokes this movie is a must see. Normally Im not into them, but my kids enjoyed the breakfast with the queen scene so much that just those two minutes justified the whole rest of the movie.All in all, the movie is quite beautiful, hits some high notes, and the kids will probably really enjoy it. I dont expect them to sell a lot of DVDs though as this doesnt seem like something that can hold up to many repeat viewings. If youre a big Roald Dahl fan, this is certainly a respectful treatment of his work, which is always good to see. Hopefully some kids will be inspired to pick up the books which remain, as always, better.

Sometimes a film grows on you over time, and thats certainly the case here. There are a couple moments that I dont like, but they are very minor. I can recall two instances where the director set up a scene by flashing to some object before the object became relevant, and in both cases the forward flashes struck me as a bit clumsy. The "wrong way" sign is the more egregious of the two accompanied as it is by a surge in the music that doesnt quite work. The "wrong way on the highway" chase scene is very good.but its impossible to do a better chase scene like that than the one in . But Ronin is overall a better movie than that one.The acting is top notch throughout. You expect greatness from Robert De Niro and he delivers and Jean Reno who is also tremendous here. Sean Bean is perfect, and Stellan Skarsgard is a revelation. Even if you dont grab it the first time, chances are the scenes will linger with you. Maybe I thought it was a little too sure of itself on the first viewing, but with reflection Ive come to realize that yes, it is that good.

I’m a little bit troubled by what I feel to be a lack of legitimate reviews on this movie. There is a very well established network of print and social media where the general public should be able to trust professional and well-educated individuals to share their honest assessment of art, literature and film without promoting a non-related agenda. Art is one of the cornerstones of civilized society, and it’s important that every artist, no matter how big or small, have their contribution judged on its own merits. I has been disturbed to witness the negative social media campaign aimed at Batman v Superman since the film’s production was announced. Most of the criticisms I have read on this film have not been of a scholarly variety, and although I do not think this film is a masterpiece” by any means, it is not a bad film, in fact I found it very interesting and thought provoking.If Batman v Superman” is only worthy of a 29 approval rating on Rottentomatoes.com, why is the viewer assessment of this film sitting at 7.210 on IMDB.com? Furthermore, the box office has been tremendous. There are indications that this film has fans, but according to my Facebook news feed, most media sources list this as a disappointment” or a train-wreck,” but, again, they do not provide scholarly arguments and rely instead on hysterical generalizations. It’s almost as if these reviews come from media sources that are owned by a corporation that produces its own rival super hero films.But let’s focus on BvS instead of conspiracies. By far the best part of this movie is Affleck as Batman. There has never been a Batman on screen quite like this. Affleck’s version is the grittiest and nastiest Batman we’ve ever seen. BvS introduces Batman as a figure terrifying to both police and criminals. The first time we see him, he’s hiding from a police officer in a ceiling very much the physical representation of a bat. When the officer happens to see Batman, he’s so scared that he fires a couple shots as Batman scurries away.Now, that is a very interesting scene and it establishes the kind of universe we’re dealing with here. In virtually every other Batman film, Batman is an aid to the police. Sometimes they work together directly, sometimes they have a kind of gentleman’s agreement. However, in BvS, Batman is clearly a vigilante that the cops are concerned about.This is a theme that hasn’t been addressed in other comic book films. Are super heroes actually heroes, or are they entities with too much power that threaten to infringe on civil liberties? I find this question interesting because it has corollaries in real life. Obviously there are no super heroes, but there are entities with power that claim to be protecting you” while arguably working towards your enslavement. How much leeway do you give entities like that? Do you let them gain power to the point where you’re essentially committing suicide simply by opposing them?Batman begins to view Superman as a threat. During the course of the film, this assessment is mainly due to the manipulation of Lex Luthor, but it remains a fascinating dynamic. Honestly, in all the negative reviews you’ve read of BvS, how many have complained that Batman wasn’t portrayed as tough enough” to handle Superman? I’ve actually seen the film, and I think the battle is quite convincing. Both Affleck and Cavill bring an almost super-human physicality to their roles.Batman comes to view his fight with Superman as his legacy” fight. He reveals this in a conversation with Alfred, played to perfection by Jeremy Irons. In another discussion with Alfred these discussions are also a highlight Batman acknowledges that he and Alfred are Criminals,” which, to me, makes him a more sympathetic Batman than others we’ve seen. One of the main criticisms of Snyder’s vision of this comic book universe is an apparent willingness for his super heroes to shed the blood of their victims. I attribute this anger to a kind of innocence fallacy” where these fans think Batman is justified in performing his acts of vigilantism as long as he does so non-lethally. The question becomes: what attacks and defenses is Batman allowed to use to appease this need? A punch to the chest can be a lethal attack, yet most fans are content to watch their superhero smash villains repeatedly. Is the line at breaking the skin? A punch to the face with draw blood from the nose, eyes, and mouth. If a villain attempts to stab Batman, can he turn the knife back on the attacker? Is Batman not allowed to shoot somebody, even if that person is about to kill an innocent party?There is always a cry to take comic books more seriously,” to perceive them as art,” to perceive them as adult.” That’s fine, but there have been dozens of comic book movies now and sooner or later some filmmaker had to amp up the realism to the point where audiences start to squirm. Snyder has given us a Batman who is aware he is a criminal, but continues on in the name of justice. Why is that an issue? Although this Batman does appear to be willing to kill his enemies, this isn’t overtly portrayed in the movie. Actually, after the backlash to Man of Steel” there is a lot of dialogue about how certain fights are happening in uninhabited areas.”Personally, I find the cartoon nature of the Avengers films to be boring. Batman V Superman” has a lot more I can sink my teeth into. Yes, there are some problems with this film, I wasn’t a big fan of Jesse Eisenberg’s performance for example. He lacked the physicality of the other leads, and had a propensity for repeating his lines off into silence blame the director and writers there. Actually there are a couple little narrative quirks like that which plague the film. Dream sequences are used too frequently. The first scene of Wayne being lifted up by bats is a divergence from the realism Snyder is otherwise determinedly pursuing. I did like the other sequence, however, featuring Superman and Batman soldiers. My other issue was the prevalence of cryptic messages scrawled or painted on: Superman’s statue, Robin’s suit, Newspaper clippings, and returned checks all in the same handwriting more or less.Overall, however, I thought this was an artistic film which was both ambitious and well-realized. It’s fun to watch Luthor brainwash the two combatants. Also, this is the first Batman film where Wayne gets a role as super detective when he sneaks around in Luthor’s mansion. I’m not sure who the figure was leaning out of the computer monitor at him at the end of the future soldier sequence, but I think that scene suggests some of Batman’s rage against Superman was the result of psychic manipulation on the part of another meta human. The denouement the BatmanSuperman battle was well conceived. Wonder Woman was also exceptionally well realized, and brought a shot of life and humor into the movie.The long and short of it is that there is plenty in Batman V Superman that is worthy of sincere critical discussion. I’m disappointed to think we live in a society where all reviews are bought and paid for and serve only the purpose of corporate agenda instead of overall greater human awareness and understanding as sometimes seems to be the case.

Now, thats how you do a relaunch, or sequel, or whatever you want to call it! Tom Hardy isnt quite Mel Gibson, but hes close, and this movie is superior to the other Mad Max films on a technical level. For all intents and purposes, this is a remake of "The Road Warrior" or "Mad Max 2" depending on what side of the pond you reside. If youre going to revisit a Mad Max film, thats the one to see. This is another one of those franchises that sails along predominantly on the success of only one of its entries.Dont be too freaked out if you cant comprehend the plot. There really isnt much of a plot beyond chase, chase, and more chase. Heck, even watching the other Mad Max films isnt going to orient you any better because there isnt complete consistency with the rules of the world. Even actors who are killed off in previous versions come back playing similar characters only to not be recognized.The way Ive made sense of the Mad Max mythology is to think of it as a very stylized version of Hell. The world seems to exist only to torment people, and torment seems eternal. Max himself manages to rise above the general miserableness.although hes not immune to it. This vague scenario allows for the filmmakers to throw in comments on society basically at will. Its the social commentary that connects this apocalyptic vision to reality and gives it some weight. But dont focus on it too hard or youll miss the fun.If youve never seen a Mad Max movie, start here, then go Road Warrior, Thunderdome, and then the original.
